t: The first day, 1 July 1916, cost the British 57,470 casualties, 19,240 of them killed, the worst in the history of the British Army, most of them north of the Albert–Bapaume road; the French Sixth Army lost 1,590.

The plan changed as the war went on: Verdun drew off French divisions, so the offensive in which the French were to take the main part became a mainly British effort, and a hoped-for decisive victory was reduced to relieving Verdun and wearing down the German army.
Casualty counts are disputed: British 419,654 to 432,000, French about 200,000, and German anywhere from 400,000 to 680,000 depending on the historian and the method of counting.
dyk: Before the attack on 1 July the British artillery fired more than 1.5 million shells in the preliminary bombardment, more than in the first year of the war, and the guns could be heard on Hampstead Heath, 165 miles (266 km) away.
ev: The Chantilly Conference agrees simultaneous Allied offensives for 1916 and the Franco-British contribution is planned for the Somme
The German attack on Verdun begins on 21 February and French divisions meant for the Somme are diverted there
On 1 July the British Fourth Army and the French Sixth Army attack the German Second Army after a bombardment that began on 24 June
On 14 July the Fourth Army attacks the German second position at Bazentin Ridge after a five-minute hurricane bombardment
On 15 September tanks, the Canadian Corps and the New Zealand Division make their debut on the Somme at Flers–Courcelette
The last big British operation of the year, the Battle of the Ancre, is fought from 13 to 18 November
British attacks on the Ancre from January force local German withdrawals, followed by Operation Alberich and the retirement to the Hindenburg Line from 16 March

f.place: Both sides of the upper reaches of the river Somme in Picardy, northern France
f.sides: The British Fourth Army under Sir Henry Rawlinson, with the Third Army and later the Reserve Army under Hubert Gough, and the French Sixth Army under Émile Fayolle, under the overall direction of Douglas Haig and Joseph Joffre, against the German Second Army under Fritz von Below; more than three million men fought in all
f.outcome: The Allies advanced about 10 km along most of the front, their largest gain since the Marne in 1914, but did not take Péronne or Bapaume; casualties on all sides exceeded one million, and the German army withdrew to the Hindenburg Line in March 1917.
